title: Probabilistic region circuit-breaker using p50/p95 and network-health signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a probabilistic region-level circuit-breaker that combines latency percentiles (p50 / p95) with network health signals (packet loss, TCP retransmits, jitter) to drive per-request routing probabilities and safe automatic fallbacks to alternate regions or model variants. This ticket produces the scoring function, configuration knobs, runtime integration, and rollout plan for the first-pass implementation.
background: Current region selection uses deterministic thresholds on latency histograms and a simple network health flag. We observe oscillation during transient congestion and noisy behavior for short-lived spikes. We also lack an automated, smooth way to reduce traffic to a region before a full failover. A probabilistic circuit-breaker that uses smoothed percentile signals and additive network health penalties should reduce oscillation, enable tactical throttling per-tier, and provide a better path for graceful degradation to lower-cost model variants or different capacity tiers.
technical_approach: 1) Signals: ingest p50 and p95 over 1m/5m windows, packet loss rate, TCP retransmit rate, and a binary upstream connectivity flag. 2) Scoring: normalize percentiles to a 0-1 latency score (with configurable baselines per-region), compute a network penalty from packet loss and retransmits, then combine as composite_score = alpha * latency_score + beta * penalty + gamma * jitter_score. 3) Probabilistic routing: map composite_score to a drop probability using a logistic function with hysteresis and emergency floor/ceiling. The final per-request routing probability to a region = capacity_adjustment * (1 - drop_probability). 4) Circuit-breaker modes: observe-only (dry-run), throttling (percent traffic reduction), and open (route 0 traffic except emergency fallbacks). 5) Fallback selection: prefer same-tier model variant if available, otherwise next available region that meets minimum composite_score threshold. 6) Telemetry and audits: emit reason codes for every routed request: LATENCY_SPIKE, NET_PENALTY, CAPACITY_LIMIT, FALLBACK_MODEL, etc.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Using p50+p95 provides short-term and tail latency signals; however, extreme tail-only triggers can be noisy. We add a minimum sample threshold to avoid acting on low-volume artifacts.
- We choose logistic mapping for smooth transitions; alternatives considered: step thresholds and linear clamps. Smooth mapping reduces oscillation but can leave some degraded requests on the region longer.
- Network signals are noisy but valuable for preemptive actions; we use exponential decay windows for packet loss to both detect bursts and forget older events.
- Capacity adjustment multiplies the routing probability, enabling us to combine circuit-breaking with explicit capacity-based throttling from Dedicated pools.
rollout_plan: 1) Lab: implement scoring function behind a feature flag and run traffic shadowing for two weeks. 2) Canary: enable observe-only mode for 1% of traffic in a single region (eu-west) and collect metrics. 3) Throttle: enable probabilistic throttling at 5% for 2 regions; validate SLOs and customer impact. 4) Gradual ramp: increase to 25% then 50% while monitoring error budgets and latency regressions. 5) Full: allow automated open mode only after manual approval. Rollback path: flip feature flag, revert routing table. All steps require a preflight checklist in PR and runbook updates.
metrics_and_slo_checks: Track: per-region p50/p95, packet_loss, retransmits, routing_probability, fallback_rate, request_success_rate, error_rate, mean_cost_per_token. SLO gates: no >2x increase in 5m error rate for production workloads during canary; fallback_rate must be <1% baseline for non-impaired regions. Set auto-pause if error_rate breach persists >3 minutes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and mapping functions; integration test with synthetic telemetry in staging to validate sample thresholding and hysteresis; chaos tests to simulate packet loss and verify graceful throttling; A/B experiment comparing deterministic threshold routing vs probabilistic circuit-breaker for oscillation and customer impact.
observability_and_dashboards: Create per-region dashboard: composite_score heatmap, routing_probability trend, fallback_reason breakdown, sample_count for percentiles, and a single-pane status with canary groups. Add a tracing tag on each routed request with score and reason code. Instrument alerting: composite_score > 0.8 for 3m triggers paging; sudden fallback_rate spike >0.5% in 5m paged to oncall.
api_and_config: Expose feature flags and per-region parameters in runtime config: baseline_latency_ms, alpha/beta/gamma weights, logistic_slope/knee, sample_threshold, decay_time_seconds, emergency_floor/ceiling. Allow per-customer tier overrides and a UI in Console under 'Routing -> Region policies' to preview probability curves.
security_and_compliance_notes: No customer data required for scoring; telemetry is aggregated. Ensure telemetry pipeline continues to redact any request identifiers. Add audit log entry when automated open-mode triggers a region quiesce action.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scoring function implemented and unit-tested. 2) Feature-flagged observe-only mode can shadow traffic without affecting routing. 3) Canary run shows reduced routing oscillation vs baseline in synthetic burst tests. 4) Dashboards and alerts exist and are validated by oncall. 5) PR merged and runbook updated.
